note: SECURITY CONDITION C2 on the finding-#7 sign-off. hr_record_rejection classifies every code into c_incident (fires on the FIRST occurrence) or c_escalating (promoted to 'incident' at c_escalate_at = 50 in one user/slot/day). 'intent_mismatch' was in NEITHER, so it stayed severity 'normal' forever at any n — and the class fix in 2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-class.sql makes twelve more RPCs able to emit it. Security's ruling: it has the rate_limited PROFILE, not the incident profile — ONE is a stale retry (a reload mid-gesture, a bfcache restore, a queued request replayed after a slot switch), FIFTY in a day is a signature an honest client cannot produce, because every client site mints a fresh uuid per gesture. c_incident was considered and REJECTED: alarming on the first late retry produces a permanently-alarming detector, which is a muted one. ANCHORED exactly-once patch on the LIVE body (never a restatement — the b484-b487 lesson), idempotent, ACL captured before the replace and asserted byte-identical after (it writes hr_rejections for an ARBITRARY user id, so a client grant is a way to forge another player's abuse record). §0 fails closed without 2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-class.sql by name. §3 PROVES the behaviour in an HR822-rolled-back block with the control that matters: ONE occurrence must stay 'normal' (a test that only checked the flip would pass identically if the code had been mis-filed into c_incident) and the FIFTIETH must read 'incident'. Zero cost: hr_rejections is already upserted on (user_id, slot, day, code) and pruned at 180 days; this changes a string in a CASE on a write that already happens. Reversible by re-applying the authoring migration or swapping the arrays back.
